title: Day 3 / 500 — ATS-Y1-003 Verify the Java main() Launcher Contract
subtitle: Use a real survey-import launch mode to investigate main-method behavior.

steps.title: Day 3.1 Verify Day 2 remote SHA and existing source
steps.why: Verify the Day 2 commit and inspect the current source before touching the launcher behavior. The runtime diagnostics already exist and must remain intact; Day 3 should add only the new startup requirement.

steps.title: Day 3.2 Read startup mode from String[] args
steps.why: Give the existing command-line argument array a real project responsibility by using it to receive a startup mode for survey import work. The goal is to connect the Java launcher contract to an operational requirement instead of treating arguments as disconnected syntax.

steps.title: Day 3.3 Add a controlled main-method contract probe
steps.why: Create a separate launcher-contract probe for controlled experiments. Keeping these experiments outside the main application lets us test unusual main-method signatures without damaging the real project flow.

steps.title: Day 3.4 Prove the launcher selects main(String[])
steps.why: Run the launcher probe and observe which main method Java selects automatically. This provides direct evidence of the launcher contract and separates what Java starts automatically from what application code calls manually.

steps.title: Day 3.5 Prove main() can be overloaded but overload is manual
steps.why: Inspect the overloaded main methods and confirm that overloading is legal Java. The important distinction is that an overload may exist in the class, but the Java launcher does not choose an arbitrary overload as the application entry point.

steps.title: Day 3.6 Reproduce non-static and non-public launcher failures
steps.why: Reproduce invalid launcher signatures in controlled experiments. Seeing the application fail when required launcher characteristics are removed gives a stronger understanding than simply memorizing that the main method must be public and static.

data.output: Error: Main method is not static in class MainWithoutStatic

steps.title: Day 3.7 Reproduce static-main @Override compiler failure
steps.why: Attempt the static-main override experiment and observe the compiler rejection. This establishes that the main method is static and therefore participates in method hiding rather than normal polymorphic overriding.

data.output: error: static methods cannot be annotated with @Override

steps.title: Day 3.8 Inspect Java 8 class version and method signatures
steps.why: Inspect the compiled method signatures and Java 8 class-file version. This ties the launcher experiments back to the actual compiled class and confirms that the Year 1 compatibility target is still preserved.

data.output: major version: 52\npublic static void main(java.lang.String[]);\npublic static void main(java.lang.String);

steps.title: Day 3.9 Update question coverage
steps.why: Update interview coverage for the main-method questions that were actually tested today. Previously completed JVM questions should be recorded as reinforcement rather than counted again.

steps.title: Day 3.10 Commit, push, and verify remote state
steps.why: Push one logical Day 3 change and verify the remote commit. Day 4 must begin from this verified state with the existing application, runtime report, and launcher probe already present.
